summary: AstroHealth Monitor is an interactive, multi-domain astronaut health and biomedical telemetry dashboard built for the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge. Long-duration spaceflight exposes crews to microgravity, radiation, isolation, and closed-loop environments—triggering cardiovascular deconditioning, bone mineral loss, immune suppression, and behavioral fatigue simultaneously.   Modeled on published NASA Human Research Program (HRP) evidence reports, NASA-STD-3001 standards, and NCRP Report 132 radiation limits, AstroHealth Monitor consolidates 18 physiological, psychological, and radiation biomarkers across 5 health domains into a unified interface. It tracks longitudinal drift against pre-flight baselines, flags anomalies with automated clinical alerts, and pairs warnings directly with actionable NASA HRP countermeasure protocols (ARED resistance, CEVIS cardio, light therapy, and a 14-item weekly self-assessment). By turning fragmented telemetry into clear, self-guided actions, it empowers deep-space crews to maintain peak health autonomously when Earth communication delays increase.
details:
AstroHealth Monitor is an interactive biomedical telemetry and self-monitoring web app for long-duration spaceflight, modeled on NASA Human Research Program (HRP) evidence reports, NASA-STD-3001 standards, and NCRP Report 132 radiation limits. Demonstrated via a mid-mission Artemis Gateway-1 scenario (Day 142/240), it tracks 18 physiological, behavioral, and radiation indicators across 5 health domains (Cardiovascular, Bone & Muscle, Immune, Behavioral Health, and Radiation).

Across six synchronized modules—Mission Overview, Health Domains, Clinical Alerts, Daily Action Center, Self-Assessment (14-item Likert check-in), and Radiation Monitor—the app tracks longitudinal drift against pre-flight baselines, computes an Overall Health Index (71/100), flags anomalies, and pairs warnings directly with actionable HRP countermeasure protocols (ARED resistance, CEVIS cardio, 10,000-lux light therapy, and supplements).

Benefits, Impact & Tech Stack By turning fragmented telemetry into closed-loop countermeasures, AstroHealth Monitor supports deep-space crew autonomy during Earth communication delays and reduces flight-surgeon cognitive load—while offering direct spin-off value for remote telemedicine and ICU monitoring. Built with React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Recharts in a low-fatigue dark glassmorphism UI, it runs offline-ready without backend dependencies
dataRefs: Whole Blood Measurements from the SpaceX Inspiration4 Mission (RNA-seq, epitranscriptome, WGS, clonal hematopoiesis, CBC)
